The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to achieve disentanglement in the wild, we need to move away from the assumption that the true generative process of the data is known.

, in order to disentangle a set of factors that describe a real world image distribution, it is not necessary to annotate the true generative attributes, but rather, it is sufficient to annotate a set that is only partially labeled.
, while it is infeasable to enumerate all possible factors in a real-world image domain, it may be possible to disentangle a subset of factors with minimal supervision.
